title: Transformer Rectifier Unit and Output Bus Bar — Installation

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Installation of the output bus bar assembly and the transformer rectifier unit, with the terminal torque sequence, the bonding measurement and the thermographic survey that closes the task out.

sections.purpose: This task installs the output bus bar assembly and the transformer rectifier unit, sets the terminal joints to the correct preload and proves the installation electrically and thermally before the bay is closed.
sections.job_setup_note: Do not start until the removal task is signed off and the bay is dry and free of swarf. The torque wrench must be calibrated within the last twelve months and the calibration record must be available. The thermographic survey at the end needs the aircraft on ground power for thirty minutes, so plan the manpower for it before you begin.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the battery is still disconnected and that the terminals are capped. 2. Clean every terminal land with a lint-free cloth and the approved solvent, and let it dry. Do not abrade a plated land. 3. Put the bus bar D2430110204063 in position and start every terminal bolt by hand. CAUTION: START ALL BOLTS BY HAND BEFORE ANY IS TORQUED. A BUS BAR PULLED DOWN ON ONE CORNER WILL NOT SEAT. 4. Fit the Belleville stacks in the orientation shown in the illustration and torque the terminals in the sequence given, in two passes. 5. Install the relay kit GIDE140223-63 on its bracket and connect it. 6. Install the backshell PE30449-35 at the outboard feed and terminate the harness screen on the bus bar housing. 7. Clean the ground stud 1GX3 face and install the strap. Measure the bonding resistance and record it. 8. Lift the unit into position with the cradle and install the four attachment bolts to the torque given. 9. Connect the input and output connectors and lock them. 10. Reset the contactor 169XU and the circuit breaker 17XU and remove the tags. 11. Reconnect the battery and restore ground power. 12. Do the direct current generation operational test. 13. WARNING: DO NOT TOUCH THE UNIT CASE OR THE BUS BAR DURING THE THERMOGRAPHIC SURVEY. Run the aircraft on ground power at full rectifier output for thirty minutes and survey every terminal. No joint may exceed the ambient by more than the figure in the limits table.
sections.close_out: Record the terminal torques, the bonding resistance and the highest terminal temperature from the survey. Close the floor panel and the access panels. Return the removed relay assembly to stores with the aircraft registration and the running hours marked on the tag.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; the Belleville stack orientation of step 4 applies only post modification

safety_precautions: Keep the battery disconnected until step 11.
Do not touch the bus bar during the thermographic survey.
